name: Jotham
charge: Preparing his ways before the Lord his God; doing according to all that his father Uzziah did, howbeit he entered not into the temple of the Lord
summary: Jotham, son of Uzziah, reigned sixteen years and did right as his father had done, but he did not go into the temple as his father had; the people still did corruptly (2 Chronicles 27:1-2). He built the high gate of the house of the Lord, cities, castles and towers, and put the Ammonites under tribute (2 Chronicles 27:3-5). He became mighty because he prepared his ways before the Lord his God (2 Chronicles 27:6).
offenseFull: Jotham judged the people from the king’s house while his father lived as a leper in a separate house, so the last years counted to Uzziah were really his son’s (2 Chronicles 26:21). He was twenty-five when he began to reign in his own right and reigned sixteen years; he did right according to all his father Uzziah did, except that he did not enter the temple of the Lord (2 Chronicles 27:1-2). He was like his father, industrious and a builder, but he did not make his father’s mistake of going in to burn incense as though he were a Levitical priest.

Yet the people still did corruptly (2 Chronicles 27:2). The high places were not removed, and the people still sacrificed and burned incense there (2 Kings 15:35); since Solomon brought in the gods of his wives, the land was never the same. Micah began to prophesy in the days of Jotham, and this is the corruption he describes: they built up Zion with blood and Jerusalem with iniquity, the heads judged for reward, the priests taught for hire, the prophets divined for money, and still they leaned on the Lord and said no evil could come on them; therefore Zion would be ploughed as a field (Micah 1:1; Micah 3:10-12). A righteous king in Jerusalem did not mean the whole realm was clean, any more than the lower parts of the capital are clean today.

He built the high gate of the house of the Lord and much on the wall of Ophel, and cities in the mountains of Judah, and castles and towers in the forests (2 Chronicles 27:3-4). He cut down the forests and made towns; we always built castles, that is Judah. He fought the king of the Ammonites and prevailed, and they paid him a hundred talents of silver and ten thousand measures each of wheat and barley that year and the next two, putting the heathen under tribute as his father had done (2 Chronicles 27:5).
judgmentFull: So Jotham became mighty, because he prepared his ways before the Lord his God (2 Chronicles 27:6). That is what Ezra did when he prepared his heart to seek the law of the Lord, to do it, and to teach it in Israel (Ezra 7:10), and it is the opposite of Rehoboam, who did evil because he did not prepare his heart to seek the Lord (2 Chronicles 12:14). That is why he had favour during his reign. The Most High was with our forefathers when they followed the commandments.

In those days the Lord began to send Rezin king of Syria and Pekah the son of Remaliah against Judah (2 Kings 15:37). Syria had been the northern kingdom’s oppressor, and now the two were joining against Judah; it began under Jotham and came to its height under his son. Jotham slept with his fathers and was buried in the city of David, not in the field where his leper father lay, and Ahaz his son reigned in his place (2 Chronicles 27:7-9). A good reign does not pass to the next by blood, and the son who followed him would burn his children in the fire.

text.text: Jotham was twenty and five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name also was Jerushah, the daughter of Zadok.
And he did that which was right in the sight of the Lord, according to all that his father Uzziah did: howbeit he entered not into the temple of the Lord. And the people did yet corruptly.
He built the high gate of the house of the Lord, and on the wall of Ophel he built much.
Moreover he built cities in the mountains of Judah, and in the forests he built castles and towers.

He fought also with the king of the Ammonites, and prevailed against them. And the children of Ammon gave him the same year an hundred talents of silver, and ten thousand measures of wheat, and ten thousand of barley. So much did the children of Ammon pay unto him, both the second year, and the third.
So Jotham became mighty, because he prepared his ways before the Lord his God.

And Uzziah the king was a leper unto the day of his death, and dwelt in a several house, being a leper; for he was cut off from the house of the Lord: and Jotham his son was over the king’s house, judging the people of the land.

The word of the Lord that came to Micah the Morasthite in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, which he saw concerning Samaria and Jerusalem.
They build up Zion with blood, and Jerusalem with iniquity.

The heads thereof judge for reward, and the priests thereof teach for hire, and the prophets thereof divine for money: yet will they lean upon the Lord, and say, Is not the Lord among us? none evil can come upon us.
Therefore shall Zion for your sake be plowed as a field, and Jerusalem shall become heaps, and the mountain of the house as the high places of the forest.
He built the high gate of the house of the Lord, and on the wall of Ophel he built much.
Moreover he built cities in the mountains of Judah, and in the forests he built castles and towers.

He fought also with the king of the Ammonites, and prevailed against them. And the children of Ammon gave him the same year an hundred talents of silver, and ten thousand measures of wheat, and ten thousand of barley. So much did the children of Ammon pay unto him, both the second year, and the third.
For Ezra had prepared his heart to seek the law of the Lord, and to do it, and to teach in Israel statutes and judgments.
And he did evil, because he prepared not his heart to seek the Lord.
In those days the Lord began to send against Judah Rezin the king of Syria, and Pekah the son of Remaliah.

In the second year of Pekah the son of Remaliah king of Israel began Jotham the son of Uzziah king of Judah to reign.

And he did that which was right in the sight of the Lord: he did according to all that his father Uzziah had done.

But when he was strong, his heart was lifted up to his destruction: for he transgressed against the Lord his God, and went into the temple of the Lord to burn incense upon the altar of incense.
And Azariah the priest went in after him, and with him fourscore priests of the Lord, that were valiant men:

And they withstood Uzziah the king, and said unto him, It appertaineth not unto thee, Uzziah, to burn incense unto the Lord, but to the priests the sons of Aaron, that are consecrated to burn incense: go out of the sanctuary; for thou hast trespassed; neither shall it be for thine honour from the Lord God.

Then Uzziah was wroth, and had a censer in his hand to burn incense: and while he was wroth with the priests, the leprosy even rose up in his forehead before the priests in the house of the Lord, from beside the incense altar.

And Azariah the chief priest, and all the priests, looked upon him, and, behold, he was leprous in his forehead, and they thrust him out from thence; yea, himself hasted also to go out, because the Lord had smitten him.
